entries.name: Avalonia
entries.use_for: Build native cross-platform desktop apps in C# and XAML.
entries.why: Leading cross-platform .NET UI framework (Windows, macOS, Linux), often used as a WPF successor.

entries.name: Eclipse Theia
entries.use_for: Framework for building custom desktop and cloud IDEs and tools
entries.why: Eclipse-governed IDE platform supporting VS Code extensions; basis for products like Arduino IDE 2; EPL-2.0.

entries.name: egui
entries.use_for: Easy immediate-mode GUI for Rust that runs natively and on the web
entries.why: The most popular Rust GUI library; fast to build tools and runs on desktop and WASM

entries.name: Electron
entries.use_for: Build cross-platform desktop apps with HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
entries.why: Powers VS Code, Slack and Discord; the most mature web-tech desktop framework with a huge ecosystem.

entries.name: Electron Forge
entries.use_for: Official all-in-one tool to scaffold, package, sign and publish Electron apps
entries.why: The Electron team's recommended build pipeline with Vite/Webpack templates and makers for every OS

entries.name: electron-builder
entries.use_for: Package, sign and publish Electron apps as installers with auto-update support.
entries.why: The standard Electron packaging tool: DMG, NSIS, AppImage, Snap and more, plus code signing and electron-updater.

entries.name: electron-vite
entries.use_for: Vite-based build tooling for Electron main, preload and renderer processes
entries.why: Fast HMR-based dev setup for Electron with sensible defaults; widely used for modern Electron apps

entries.name: Flet
entries.use_for: Build desktop, web and mobile apps in Python with Flutter-rendered UI
entries.why: Easiest way to ship cross-platform GUIs from Python without frontend experience

entries.name: Fyne
entries.use_for: Cross-platform GUI toolkit for Go: desktop and mobile from one codebase
entries.why: The most popular Go GUI toolkit; material-style widgets and simple packaging

entries.name: iced
entries.use_for: Cross-platform Elm-inspired GUI library for Rust
entries.why: Leading Rust native GUI toolkit; used by System76's COSMIC desktop

entries.name: Neutralinojs
entries.use_for: Lightweight cross-platform desktop apps with JS, HTML and CSS using the system webview
entries.why: Tiny binaries without bundling Chromium or Node; language-agnostic extensions

license_verified.note: Core MIT; bundled third-party libraries keep their own permissive licenses

entries.name: NW.js
entries.use_for: Build desktop apps with HTML, CSS and JS with Node.js APIs available in the DOM
entries.why: Long-standing Electron alternative with direct Node access from web pages and source protection

entries.name: Pake
entries.use_for: Wrap an existing website into a lightweight desktop app with one command.
entries.why: Tauri-based CLI that produces small native apps (~5 MB) from a URL; far lighter than Electron wrappers.

entries.name: PakePlus
entries.use_for: Package any webpage or web app into a small desktop/mobile app
entries.why: Tauri-based wrapper producing ~5MB apps from a URL or HTML build, with GUI and CI builds; MIT.

entries.name: pywebview
entries.use_for: Lightweight wrapper to show HTML UIs in a native webview window from Python
entries.why: The go-to way to build web-UI desktop apps in Python with a JS-Python bridge

entries.name: Slint
entries.use_for: Declarative UI toolkit for native desktop, embedded and mobile apps from Rust, C++, JS or Python
entries.why: Native UI with its own markup language; GPL-3.0, royalty-free and commercial options

license_verified.note: Triple-licensed: GPL-3.0-only, Slint Royalty-free 2.0 (proprietary desktop/mobile/web, not embedded) or commercial

entries.name: Tauri
entries.use_for: Build small, secure desktop (and mobile) apps with a web frontend and a Rust backend.
entries.why: Uses the OS webview instead of bundling Chromium, so binaries are a few MB; strong security model and plugin system.

entries.name: Wails
entries.use_for: Build desktop apps with a Go backend and any web frontend.
entries.why: Go equivalent of Tauri: native webview, generated TS bindings to Go methods and small binaries.
